title: Approximation by a simple polynomial root over a dense subfield
statement: Let $K\hookrightarrow L$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with nontrivial valuations [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Suppose the image of $K$ is dense in $L$ and its valuation topology is the induced topology. Assume the valuation ring of $L$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $L^s/L$ be a separable closure [def-kun-separably-closed], with compatible $K$-algebra structure. For every $a\in L^s$, there are a monic polynomial $g\in K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and an element $b\in L^s$ with $g(b)=0$, $g^{\prime}(b)\ne0$, and $a\in L(b)$, the intermediate field generated by $b$. Henselianity of $K$ is not required, and no separable closure of $K$ is part of the statement.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a finite Galois extension N/L inside Ls containing a. Prolong the valuation of L to N; its valuation ring is henselian and the induced topology on L is the given one. Let f be the monic minimal polynomial of a over L. Its degree is positive and its separability implies f'(a) is nonzero by evaluating a Bezout identity for f and f'.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: Take a Krasner neighbourhood U of a in N. Simple-root stability for f over the henselian valued field N gives an open coefficient neighbourhood V such that every monic polynomial of the same degree with coefficients in V has a simple root in U. Pull V back to the finite product of L. Its preimage is open and contains the coefficient tuple of f. Choose a product-basic neighbourhood inside it; density of K in L chooses a K coefficient in each of these finitely many neighbourhoods.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: The chosen coefficients define a monic g over K. By stability it has a simple root b in U, so g(b)=0 and g'(b) is nonzero. Krasner gives a in L(b). Map N into Ls to obtain the required conclusion there. If a is in L, one may alternatively choose g=X and b=0, since L(0)=L. Thus degree one and zero cause no exception.

theorem denseHenselian_exists_simple_root
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    (Γ : Type v) (Δ : Type w)
    [LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero Γ] [LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero Δ]
    [vK : Valued K Γ] [vL : Valued L Δ]
    [vK.v.IsNontrivial] [vL.v.IsNontrivial]
    [HenselianLocalRing vL.v.valuationSubring]
    (h_induced : Topology.IsInducing (algebraMap K L))
    (h_dense : DenseRange (algebraMap K L))
    (Ls : Type t) [Field Ls] [Algebra L Ls] [IsSepClosure L Ls]
    [Algebra K Ls] [IsScalarTower K L Ls] (a : Ls) :
    ∃ (g : Polynomial K) (b : Ls), g.Monic ∧
      Polynomial.aeval b g = 0 ∧ Polynomial.aeval b g.derivative ≠ 0 ∧
      a ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin L {b}
